subject: Post-call follow-up: ephemeral archive waiver & pilot options
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Brooks <olivia.brooks@hospitalchain.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call follow-up: ephemeral archive waiver & pilot options

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

What we heard from HospitalChain:
- Primary ask: avoid persisting any identifiable patient PII from model inputs/outputs in long-term logs; preference for ephemeral-only storage for PII-bearing requests where possible.
- Compliance constraint: auditability for safety/incident cases — you need a defensible path for short-term forensic access and a clear revocation/consent process.
- Residency: must be hosted in us-east-1 for the pilot.

Redwood options we proposed (summary):
- Option A — Ephemeral archival waiver (pilot): keep full request/response KV for 24 hours, then auto-purge; token-level redaction for common PHI patterns; encrypted short-lived archive for incidents with signed request by HospitalChain SOC (7-day hold for approved incidents only).
- Option B — Minimal telemetry: store only non-PII telemetry and model traces for 7 days (no request/response retention).

Attachments I shared: SOC2-Type2-2026.pdf and an architecture diagram showing the ephemeral path.

Immediate asks from HospitalChain: sample DPA clause for the 24-hour ephemeral pilot, and confirmation that we can restrict residency to us-east-1 and provide auditable deletion logs.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I will send a short DPA addendum draft for the ephemeral pilot (attached).
2) Marissa can run a quick feasibility check and confirm token-redaction limits and expected false-positive rate.
3) If the pilot approach looks good, schedule a technical deep-dive next week to validate workload and rollout plan.

Proposed timeline: quick pilot in 2–3 weeks, followed by eval and narrow rollout.

If that sounds right, I'll loop in Aditya to put a pilot statement of work on the HubSpot deal and circulate the DPA draft.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Brooks <olivia.brooks@hospitalchain.com>

Cc: security@hospitalchain.com, Matthew Chen <matthew.chen@hospitalchain.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T11:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: ephemeral archive waiver & pilot options

Thanks, Mina — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our side before we sign off on a pilot: 

1) Token-level redaction: can you describe which PHI patterns you redact by default (SSNs, MRNs, DOBs, free-text names) and whether we can add custom regexes? What's the estimated recall/precision for the redaction model?
2) Audit access: for authorized incident review, how do you ensure the short-lived archive is only accessible after a signed request? We need paper trail + automatic expiry.
3) Residency: is us-east-1 exclusive for the pilot (no cross-region backup)?

I've attached our security questionnaire (HC-Security-Questionnaire.xlsx) — some of the asks are table-driven and map to SOC2 controls. Also copying our CISO (matthew.chen) who will want a short legal/ops summary.

Olivia
Olivia Brooks
Director, Digital Innovation | HospitalChain Health
olivia.brooks@hospitalchain.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Brooks <olivia.brooks@hospitalchain.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: ephemeral archive waiver & pilot options

Hi Olivia — answers inline and a concrete pilot proposal attached. Short version: yes to all items with two alternative guardrail configurations depending on risk appetite.

1) Redaction: default PHI detectors cover SSNs, MRNs, credit card numbers, ISO-date DOB detection, and NER for person names. We can add custom regexes; typical recall for the pattern-based rules is ~99% for structured identifiers and ~88–92% for name/entity NER (depends on free-text entropy). We'll include a false-positive suppression list to avoid over-redaction for clinical shorthand.

2) Audit access: access to the short-lived encrypted archive is gated by an HMAC-signed request token and an approval workflow that logs the requestor, purpose, and timestamp. Retrieval generates an immutable audit entry that we can export as CSV. Auto-purge runs after 24 hours (Option A) unless an approved incident hold is placed — holds require a signed request and are limited to 7 days for containment/investigation.

3) Residency: we can restrict pilot data to us-east-1 with no asynchronous cross-region backups; backups can be disabled for the pilot environment.

Two pilot configurations (choose one):
- Option A (recommended for product parity): 24-hour KV retention with token redaction + incident hold process (7-day max hold). Provides full fidelity for debugging for a limited window.
- Option B (privacy-first): no request/response retention, only aggregated non-PII telemetry for 7 days. Reduced debug capability.

Attached: proposed-ephemeral-waiver-dpa-draft.docx (legal language for the addendum) and a short runbook for how incident holds are requested.

If HospitalChain is comfortable with Option A, we can start the pilot in a stacked environment — Marissa to confirm exact rollout steps and instrumentation. I'll put this into HubSpot (deal HC-2026-004) after you confirm.

Thanks,
Mina

On a related note: Ben, can you share the expected unit pricing impact for 24-hour retention vs. no-retention? Aditya — please hold an SOW template we can reuse for pilot procurement.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call follow-up: ephemeral archive waiver & pilot options

Hi Olivia — quick feasibility note from platform/ops:
- We can implement token-level redaction rules and add custom regex on request. We'll validate examples you provide during the deep-dive.
- Pilots can be provisioned in us-east-1 with backups disabled.
- For incident holds, platform automatically snapshots the minimal encrypted artifact and logs the approval metadata. We will include a retrieval playbook and reviewer access matrix.

Timeline for a minimal pilot: provision environment (3 business days), deploy config + redaction rules (2 business days), run smoke tests and sign-off (2 business days). Total ~7–8 business days from confirmation.

I'll bring the runbook and the ephemeral-architecture-diagram to the technical deep-dive.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
